 (P. SHIVARAJ)
 Vth Addl. S.C.Judge & XXIVth ACJM  SCCH-20, Mayohall Unit, Bangalore  2 MVC No.4354/2024  JUDGMENT Petitioner has filed this petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming the compensation amount of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.

2. Petitioner case is as Follows:
Subramani M vs Muniraju on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180932908/
1

sentences.text:
That on 21.04.2024 at about 5.30 am, he was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg No.KA-53-EU-7401, in Chinthamani Hosakote road, near Cholappanahalli Gate,
Petrol Bunk, wherein the driver of the Vehicle beg.
Reg . No.KA-03-MV-8534 drove it with high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the two wheeler from its behind and caused the accident.
In the said accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

He took first aid at Srinivasapura Govt Hospital, later he was shifted to the Srinivasa Speciality Hospital, Hosakote, wherein he took treatment as inpatient for the accidental injuries and he spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards his medical expenses,
Petitioner stated that Prior to the accident he was hale and healthy and he is aged about 43 years and he was working as an electrician and thereby he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

Further petitioner stated that the jurisdictional police have registered Cr.No.128/2024 against the driver and owner of the offending vehicle as the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver.
Petitioner stated that respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle and he is responsible to pay the compensation with interest.
He prays this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.
3. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondent, Respondent has appeared through his counsel filed vakalath and written statement.
He contended that accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.
4. Petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and examined two witness as PW-2 and PW-3 and got marked 23 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 23.

Respondent has not chosen cross examine the PW.1 to 3, though their application was allowed on two occasion, inasmuch considering the conduct and approach of the respondent cross examination of PW.1 to 3 is taken as nil.
Respondent he has not chosen to lead the evidence hence respondent evidence is taken as nil.
Respondent filed memo along with the documents stating that he has paid Rs.50,000/- to the petitioner.
The said fact is admitted by the petitioner.
5. I have heard the arguments for the counsel appearing for both the sides and I have perused the entire records.

6. On the basis of pleadings my learned predecessor in office has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.Whether the petitioner proves that on 21.04.2024 at about 5.30 am, he was riding motorcycle bearing Reg No.KA-53-EU-7401, in Chinthamani Hosakote road, near Cholappanahalli Gate, Petrol Bunk, wherein the driver of the Vehicle beg.
Reg.No.KA-03- MV-8534 drove it with high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the two wheeler from its behind and caused the accident.

In the said accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries Subramani M vs Muniraju on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180932908/
2 as alleged in the petition.?

2.Whether respondent proves that accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner, and he has already settled the claim as contended at para of the written statement.?
3.Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
4.
What order or award?

7. After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
 Issue no.1: In the affirmative,
 Issue no.2: In the negative,
 Issue no.3: In Partly Affirmative  Issue no.4: As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 8. Issue No.1 & 2 :- I have taken these issues together for common discussion so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW1 being the petitioner, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.

Petitioner has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, police intimation,
mahazar, IMV report, final report, Notice U/s 133 of MV Act and reply notice which are at Ex.P.1 to 10.
9.

On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents it is evident that one Prathap s/o Babu was the driver of the offending vehicle and the accident took place due to his rash and negligent driving.

Ex.P.9 is the reply notice given by the respondent, to the notice issued by the police under section 133 of M.V.Act, wherein he admitted that Prathap was the driving the vehicle as on the date of the accident and he was having valid driving license.
Further he admitted that his vehicle is not covered under the valid insurance policy as on the date of the accident.

The final report which is at Ex.P10 is filed after the through investigation and it is the prima facie proof of the accident and the involvement of the offending vehicle and rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and its owner, further it is true as per the final report that respondent has violated the section 196 of IMV Act.

The alleged negligent act of the petitioner is not probabilised as contended in the written statement and the respondent has not chosen to cross examine the Pw- 1 to 3 and he has not chosen to lead the evidence.
The conduct of the respondent establishes that he has accepted his guilt and his liability.
10. Petitioner has tender the wound certificate, discharge summary as per Ex.P.6 & 11.

The aforesaid documents shows that the petitioner has sustained simple and grievous injuries that is right side distal tibia fibula fracture and CRIF with nailing was done by way of surgery on 21.04.2024.

It is true that petitioner took treatment as an inpatient for 3 days and he has spent medical expenses of Subramani M vs Muniraju on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180932908/
3 Rs.1,60,937/- as per Ex.P.15.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following heads.

Pecuniary damages (Medical expenses) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, Medicines,
Transportation, Nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure:
11.
Petitioner took treatment at Srinivasa Speciality hospital, Hosakote.
He has tendered the wound certificate, discharge summary and medical bills and reports along with the related documents.
On perusal of the same it is apparent that, petitioner has incurred Rs.1,60,937/- towards actual medical expenses.
Evidently there is no material to disbelieve the medical bills.
Accordingly the wound certificate, discharge summary and the medical bills issued form the hospital has to be accepted.

Admittedly petitioner has taken treatment for 3 days, for attendant charges, transportation,
nourishing food, he might have spend some more expenses.
Therefore in addition to the actual medical expenses of Rs.1,60,937/-, I award Rs.10,000/-.
In total petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,70,937/- compensation under this head.
Non-Pecuniary damages (General damages) Loss of income during laid up period.
12. The petitioner has not substantiated his nature of work and income as alleged in the petition.
Accident took place on 21.04.2024, however as per notional income chart, the notional income for the year 2024 is Rs.16,500/-, and same is assessed and considered as his monthly income.
Considering the accidental injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, I am of view that at-least 1 month he has lost his income.
Therefore I award Rs.16,500/- as compensation under this head.
Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
13. The petitioner has examined the Orthopedic surgeon Dr.S.A.Somashekar as PW-3.
He deposed that, petitioner has 21% of whole body disability as per Ex.P22.
Learned advocate for the respondent argued that the assessment of PW-3 is on higher side.
I have perused the evidence of PW-3 wound certificate, discharge summary given by both the hospitals, X-ray etc.
Evidently petitioner has not examined the doctors who have treated him in the hospital.

It is true that petitioner sustained the grievous injuries and CRIF with nailing was done way of surgery, further doctor has admitted that petitioner is able to perform his work with some effort and the fracture is united.
Admittedly petitioner is having no functional disability.
The percentage of loss of earning capacity due to accidental injuries is different from the percentage of physical disability due to accidental injuries.
Considering the medical reports and oral testimony of doctor, the whole body disability of the petitioner is assessed as 17%.
The notional monthly income of the petitioner is assessed as Rs.16,500/-, the age of petitioner as on the date of accident is 44 years as per the entry in Aadhar card which is at ExP.12 .
The multiplier applicable to this case is "14".

Therefore loss of income on account of permanent disability is calculated as follows;
Subramani M vs Muniraju on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180932908/
4 Rs.16,500/-(Monthly income) X 12 (Months) X 14 ( Multiplier) X17% (Functional Disability) =
Rs.4,71,240/-

entities.text: Subramani M vs Muniraju on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.4,71,240/- as compensation under this head.

Non-Pecuniary damages (General damages) (IV)Damages for pain and sufferings and loss of amenities:
14.
It is undisputed fact that petitioner has sustained grievous injury.
During the hospitalization and rehabilitation period, he might have undergone lot of pain and sufferings and due to accidental injuries he has forgone certain amenities available for him.
There fore I award Rs.20,000/- under these conventional heads.

V) Loss of Amenities :-
15.
The petitioner has to forego certain amenities available for him before accident.
Therefore I award Rs.20,000/- as compensation under this head.
As per the oral testimony of PW-3, another surgery is required for the petitioner, for the removal of implants.
The estimated cost of the surgery is not tendered.
Tentatively petitioner is entitled for Rs.25,000/- for the additional surgery.
16. Except these heads the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under any other heads.

In all the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:
 Sl Particulars Amount  No.
 1 Towards Medical expenses, attendant Rs.1,70,937/-
charges, transportation, nourishing food 2 Loss of income during the laid up period Rs. 16,500/- 3 Loss of income on account of Rs.4,71,240/-
permanent disability 4 pain & sufferings Rs. 20,000/-
5 loss of amenities Rs. 20,000/-
6 Cost of Additional surgery Rs.25,000/-
TOTAL Rs.7,23,677/-
17.
Rate of Interest:

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.

18. Liability: The Respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle, he has not insured his vehicle as per final report and his reply notice, Accordingly respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle he is liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the Petitioner.
Petitioner has admitted that he has received Rs.50,000/- from the respondent and the said amount Subramani M vs Muniraju on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180932908/
5 has to be deducted from the compensation amount.
Accordingly I am answering Issue No.1 in affirmative, Issue No.2 in negative and issue No.3 in partly affirmative.
19. Issue No.4;

For the foregoing reason and discussion, on point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor vehicle Act,1988, is partly allowed with cost.
Petitioner is entitled for the compensation amount of Rs.6,73,677/- with interest at the rate of 6% P.A from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this tribunal with in 30 days from the date of the judgment.
After depositing the compensation amount with interest, petitioner is permitted to withdraw the entire compensation amount with interest by comply the mandate of circular No.39/2020 dt. 17.01.2020.
Advocate fee of Rs.1000/- is fixed.
All the interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
Draw award accordingly.

(P. SHIVARAJ) Vth Addl. Judge & XXIVth ACJM SCCH-20, Mayohall Unit, Bangalore
